ai_review.summary: A superb true‑matrix recording that captures a high‑energy 1973 Boston show highlighted by a monster “Eyes of the World” and tight, soaring jams.
ai_review.review: Listeners rave about the Dusborne matrix – a seamless blend of soundboard and audience that sounds crystal‑clear and is called the best matrix they’ve heard. The performance itself is praised as one of the band’s finest of ’73, with an explosive “Eyes of the World,” powerful “Morning Dew” opener, and tight transitions throughout the 22‑song set.

ai_rating.rationale: Over a dozen detailed reviews uniformly give 4–5 stars, praising both the exceptional matrix sound and the show’s energy and standout jams.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Repeatedly described as a true matrix (soundboard overlaid with audience), crisp, extraordinary sounding, and the best matrix the reviewers have heard; no significant flaws mentioned.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows smoothly with tight transitions, especially noted from the pre‑Slipknot jam into Sugar Magnolia; the mix of newer material and classics keeps momentum high.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for his guitar tone (“Jerry and you can’t lose”) and overall performance.
band_member_comments.Bob: Highlighted for a funny “Bobby Weir” imitation during Sugar Magnolia and solid rhythm/vocal work.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith is specifically mentioned on piano, adding to the jam quality.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s jazz‑style drumming praised; reviewers note Mickey’s absence but overall drum work is well received.
